artifacts.summary: Finds that tests/run-all.sh already ships a complete --fail-on-new flag plus known-failures.txt manifest (the exact expected/NEW accounting the task asks for), and verify-deploy.sh already has a warn_advisory() primitive that is excluded from deploy_findings_snapshot's FINDING-line filter. Recommends a minimal three-way branch in gate8_run() (pass/warn_advisory/fail) requiring no code change to run-all.sh or deploy-baseline-lib.sh. Confirms task 411's gate-registry refactor is complete, so no coordination/sequencing block remains. Re-verifies all four named consumers: two are structurally unaffected (Gate 8 deferred under --skip-slow), one (orchestrate-batch-gate.sh) is the exact consumer the measured evidence describes and is fixed by the recommended design, and verify-deploy.sh's own direct-invocation output is the primary consumer named in the dispatch's evidence.

memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh has a warn_advisory() function (alongside pass()/fail()/warn()) that increments CHECKS but never FAILURES, prints a [WARN] narrative, and -- when findings mode is on -- writes a 'WARN-FINDING <gate> ...' line instead of 'FINDING <gate> ...'. deploy_findings_snapshot() (lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh) filters strictly on grep '^FINDING ', so a WARN-FINDING line is invisible to every consumer that chokepoints through that function (orchestrate-batch-gate.sh, orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's redeploy checkpoint, command-gate-out.sh). This is the sanctioned primitive for 'a gate check that must stay visible and trackable but must never become batch-blocking' -- use it instead of inventing a new severity channel.

tests/run-all.sh already has a mature expected-vs-NEW failure accounting system: a committed, advisory, basename-keyed tests/known-failures.txt manifest (format: basename|category|reason|owner), classification of each failing suite as EXPECTED or NEW, an unconditional (not --quiet-suppressed) annotated end-of-run roster and tally line (e.g. '158 passed, 1 failed (1 expected, 0 NEW), 0 skipped, 159 total'), and an opt-in --fail-on-new flag that exits 0 when every failure is EXPECTED. The roster deliberately contains zero occurrences of the literal token '[FAIL]' to avoid double-counting against the anchored [FAIL]-line extraction other tooling (verify-deploy.sh's Gate 8) uses. A caller wanting NEW-vs-EXPECTED-aware behavior should pass --fail-on-new rather than re-deriving the classification from known-failures.txt independently.
